test_scenario: Profile record counts in selected banking tables
preconditions: Sample SQLite banking database is available and accessible.
test_steps: 1. Execute the database overview query. 2. Review the row count returned for each selected table.
expected_result: The query returns a row count for each of the 8 selected tables: customers, accounts, transactions, cards, transfers, bill_payments, loans, and loan_payments.
actual_result: 1,187 records in total across the 8 selected tables; transactions contain 1,000 records.
notes: Profiling check; not a pass/fail test.

test_scenario: Check required customer fields for missing or blank values
test_steps: 1. Execute the customer completeness query. 2. Review returned records.
expected_result: No customers have a null or blank email, first name, or last name.
notes: Result is limited to the fields checked by the query.

test_scenario: Check for duplicate customer emails after normalization
test_steps: 1. Execute the duplicate email query. 2. Review any grouped results.
expected_result: No normalized email value appears more than once.
notes: Email values are trimmed and converted to lowercase before comparison.

preconditions: Accounts and customers tables are available.
test_steps: 1. Execute the account-to-customer referential integrity query. 2. Review returned account IDs.
expected_result: Every account references an existing customer.
actual_result: No accounts linked to nonexistent customers found.
notes: Checks the customer relationship used by the query.

preconditions: Accounts and branches tables are available.
test_steps: 1. Execute the account-to-branch referential integrity query. 2. Review returned account IDs.
expected_result: Every account references an existing branch.
actual_result: No accounts linked to nonexistent branches found.
notes: Checks the branch relationship used by the query.

test_steps: 1. Execute the duplicate account number query. 2. Review duplicate groups.
expected_result: No account number is associated with more than one account.
notes: Null account numbers are excluded by the query.

preconditions: Transactions and accounts tables are available.
test_steps: 1. Execute the transaction-to-account referential integrity query. 2. Review returned transaction IDs.
expected_result: Every transaction references an existing account.
actual_result: No transactions linked to nonexistent accounts found.
notes: Checks the account relationship used by the query.

test_steps: 1. Execute the transaction amount validation query. 2. Review returned transactions.
expected_result: No transaction has a null, zero, or negative amount.
actual_result: No null, zero, or negative transaction amounts found.
notes: Validation rule follows the SQL query; business rules should confirm whether all transaction types must have positive amounts.

test_scenario: Profile transaction types and amount ranges
test_steps: 1. Execute the transaction type profiling query. 2. Review counts and amount ranges by type.
expected_result: The query returns a count, minimum amount, and maximum amount for each transaction type.
notes: Descriptive profiling; amount ranges are documented in the README.

test_steps: 1. Execute the duplicate card number query. 2. Review the number of duplicate groups without exposing card numbers.
expected_result: No duplicate card-number groups, subject to the applicable business rule.
notes: Confirm whether repeated card numbers are permitted by the data model and business rules. The query excludes null card numbers.

test_scenario: Identify standing orders with past next-run dates
preconditions: Standing orders table is populated and next-run dates are parseable by SQLite.
test_steps: 1. Execute the standing order date query. 2. Review records whose next-run date is before SQLite's current date.
expected_result: No past-dated next-run records, unless such dates are allowed by business rules.
actual_result: 10 standing orders with past next-run dates found.
notes: Confirm whether these schedules are overdue or expected in the sample dataset.

test_scenario: Reconcile recorded account balances with transaction-derived balances
preconditions: Accounts and transactions tables are available; reconciliation assumptions are documented.
test_steps: 1. Calculate each account balance from transaction types. 2. Compare the calculated balance with the recorded balance. 3. Review differences greater than 0.01.
expected_result: No absolute balance difference greater than 0.01, under the stated assumptions.
actual_result: No balance mismatches returned across 20 accounts.
notes: Assumes zero opening balances, complete transaction history, deposits and interest increase balances, and withdrawals and fees decrease balances.
